correctness.rationale: For all fixed N>=2 and s>0, the disc Toeplitz spectrum is strictly decreasing with gap b_N(s)>0. The rank-one coherent-state boundary integral has four trace-norm derivatives at the positive boundary. Its first derivative is sqrt(b_j b_k) times the angular Fourier coefficient; its second diagonal derivative sums to -b_(N-1) times the mean square by the Poisson recurrence. The isolated top spectral projection has a standard differentiated resolvent contour, whose mixed-block terms are exactly 2*b_j*b_k/(lambda_j-lambda_k). Grouping by k-j gives the complete Fourier coefficient L_(N,m), with denominators the positive finite Poisson sums. In m=1 it cancels exactly; in m=2 the only two crossing terms reduce to the strictly positive rational coefficient in RESULT.md. Exact rotation symmetry makes the quadrupole deficit even, giving O(epsilon^4). Package code tests the exact rational identities for 75 choices and finite-matrix asymptotics for 12 cases; neither is used as an infinite proof. Limits: only local smooth shape deformations, fixed finite N and s.

originality.rationale: Abreu arXiv:2607.28376 (full publicly posted text read) proves the global Ky Fan extremal inequality and the disc eigenvalue formula, but neither its theorem nor Sections 2–5 calculate the nonradial second shape derivative, full angular Hessian, or positive closed quadrupole coefficient for rank N>=2. Earlier Nicola–Riccardi–Tilli work arXiv:2503.07069 restricts the proven isoperimetric comparison to radial sets; arXiv:2607.20965 proves existence. Earlier quantitative STFT stability is rank one. published-finding corpus and local claimed-statement searches identified no direct or stronger covering statement. Independent bibliographic verification remains unperformed and accessible-source limitations are stated below.
residual_risks: The complete text of arXiv:2503.07069 and arXiv:2607.20965 was not accessible; appendices could contain related perturbative calculations.
Published and unpublished operator-theoretic shape-derivative literature may contain an equivalent local Hessian under another normalization; semantic searches cannot rule out all overlap.
No independent mathematical or originality audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The sharp 2026 unrestricted Fock Ky Fan inequality motivates quantitative stability and equality-case analysis, but gives no exact local coefficient. The full angular Hessian for every N>=2 and every area is a structural spectral-shape statement; the translation zero mode and a strictly positive quadrupole curvature with exact rank-and-area dependence identify the first genuinely deforming direction. This positive coefficient is not a simple corollary of numerical correctness or the global sign and is useful in pursuing local spectral rigidity and quantitative stability. Only this local invariant is claimed, without an unwarranted global theorem.
